page_title: Singapore Executive Job-Search Market Research Guide

keyword_metrics.note: Search terms are hypotheses only; no volume, difficulty, or demand is asserted.

search_intent.intent: Unmeasured country-specific research hypothesis: distinguish Singapore MOM resident labour-force statistics from all-worker, vacancy and executive-specific evidence.
evidence: MOM's annual Labour Force in Singapore report covers the resident labour force; its summary table defines residents as Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

intended_audience: Senior executives and candidates researching the Singapore employment market.
geographic_relevance: Singapore only. Focuses on Ministry of Manpower resident labour-force datasets and their scope.

competitor_research.name: Singapore-localized candidate-facing search results and direct market-guide competitors
competitor_research.finding: A current Singapore-localized search-results review and direct competitor comparison was not performed.

commercial_relevance: Potential country-specific candidate research resource only if a distinct user need, demand, overlap and KOV serviceability are later established. MOM labour-force data does not establish commercial value or KOV capability.
unique_content_purpose: Help senior candidates distinguish Singapore's resident labour-force statistics from all-worker and executive hiring evidence, and understand the resident population and seasonal-adjustment notes.
duplication_and_cannibalisation_assessme: The existing Singapore Employment Pass mobility guide addresses work authorization, not interpretation of resident labour-force data. The existing executive job-search resource is jurisdiction-neutral. Full overlap and demand review remain pending; keep provisional until a distinct need is demonstrated.

authoritative_sources.title: Labour Force in Singapore 2025
authoritative_sources.research_use_and_limit: Used for annual report scope and the available labour-force, employment, income, occupation, industry and mobility sections. Figures concern the resident labour force and do not establish executive-specific demand.
